A box contains five balls of same size and shape. Three of them are green
coloured balls and two of them are orange coloured balls. Balls are drawn from
the box one at a time. If a green ball is drawn, it is not replaced. If an orange ball
is drawn, it is replaced with another orange ball.
First ball is drawn. What is the probability of getting an orange ball in the next
draw?
questions.explaination: Initially, there are 3 green and 2 orange balls (total 5). If a green ball is drawn ($P(G_1) = 3/5$), 2 green and 2 orange remain, so $P(O_2|G_1) = 2/4 = 1/2$. If an orange ball is drawn ($P(O_1) = 2/5$), it is replaced, so $P(O_2|O_1) = 2/5$. By the law of total probability, $P(O_2) = \left(\frac{3}{5}\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) + \left(\frac{2}{5}\right)\left(\frac{2}{5}\right) = \frac{3}{10} + \frac{4}{25} = \frac{23}{50}$.

P: Set of Rational numbers (positive and negative)
Q: Set of functions from {0, 1} to N
R: Set of functions from N to {0, 1}

Which of the sets above are countable?

questions.explaination: Set $P$ (rationals) is countably infinite. Set $Q$ (functions $\{0, 1\} \to \mathbb{N}$) is equivalent to $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$, which is countable. Set $R$ (functions $\mathbb{N} \to \{0, 1\}$) is equivalent to the power set $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{N})$ and has cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$, which is uncountable. Let U = {1, 2, . . . , n}, where n is a large positive integer greater than 1000. Let
k be a positive integer less than n. Let A, B be subsets of U with |A| = |B| = k
and A ∩B = ∅. We say that a permutation of U separates A from B if one of the
following is true.
- All members of A appear in the permutation before any of the members of B.
- All members of B appear in the permutation before any of the members of A.
How many permutations of U separate A from B?
questions.subtopic: Combinatorics: counting, recurrence relations, generating functions
questions.explaination: There are 2 orderings for which block appears first ($A$ before $B$ or $B$ before $A$). There are $\binom{n}{2k}$ ways to choose the positions in the permutation for elements of $A \cup B$. The first $k$ chosen positions must contain elements of the first set ($k!$ permutations) and the next $k$ positions contain elements of the second set ($k!$ permutations). The remaining $n - 2k$ elements can be arranged in any of the $(n - 2k)!$ remaining positions. Total valid permutations $= 2 \binom{n}{2k} (n - 2k)! (k!)^2$.

for i = 1, . . . , n
color(vi) ←min{j ∈N :

Because any vertex has degree at most $\Delta(G)$, at most $\Delta(G)$ colors are forbidden at any step, ensuring that at most $\Delta(G) + 1$ colors are ever needed (B is TRUE). Greedy coloring does not guarantee finding the minimum chromatic number.

proper colouring of the graph. Let 𝐺 be any graph with 𝑛 vertices and chromatic
number 𝑘. Which of the following statements is/are always TRUE?

questions.explaination: A proper $k$-coloring partitions the $n$ vertices into $k$ independent sets. By the Pigeonhole Principle, at least one of these independent sets has size $\ge \lceil n/k \rceil \ge n/k$ (B is TRUE). In addition, every pair of color classes must have at least one edge between them (otherwise those two colors could be merged, yielding a $(k-1)$-coloring), requiring at least $\binom{k}{2} = \frac{k(k-1)}{2}$ edges (C is TRUE).

questions.explaination: For $\square$: $a \square b = ab$, which is associative since $(ab)c = a(bc)$ (B is TRUE). Distributivity of $\square$ over $\diamond$: $a \square (b \diamond c) = a(b + 2c) = ab + 2ac$. Comparing with $(a \square b) \diamond (a \square c) = (ab) \diamond (ac) = ab + 2(ac) = ab + 2ac$; both sides match identically, so $\square$ distributes over $\diamond$ (D is TRUE). For $\diamond$: $(a \diamond b) \diamond c = a + 2b + 2c \neq a + 2b + 4c = a \diamond (b \diamond c)$, so $\diamond$ is not associative.

The number of edges present in the forest generated by the DFS traversal of an
undirected graph 𝐺 with 100 vertices is 40. The number of connected components
in 𝐺 is _________
questions.explaination: A DFS traversal of an undirected graph with $V$ vertices and $k$ connected components produces a spanning forest containing $k$ trees. A tree with $v_i$ vertices contains $v_i - 1$ edges, so the total number of tree edges in the forest is $\sum (v_i - 1) = V - k$. Given $V = 100$ and $E = 40$, we have $40 = 100 - k \implies k = 60$ connected components.

The instruction pipeline of a RISC processor has the following stages: Instruction Fetch (IF),
Instruction Decode (ID), Operand Fetch (OF), Perform Operation (PO) and Writeback (WB).

A processor has 16 integer registers (R0, R1, .. , R15) and 64 floating point registers (F0,
F1,… , F63). It uses a 2-byte instruction format. There are four categories of instructions:
Type-1, Type-2, Type-3, and Type-4. Type-1 category consists of four instructions, each
with 3 integer register operands (3Rs). Type-2 category consists of eight instructions, each
with 2 floating point register operands (2Fs). Type-3 category consists of fourteen
instructions, each with one integer register operand and one floating point register operand
(1R+1F). Type-4 category consists of N instructions, each with a floating point register
operand (1F).

The maximum value of N is __________.
questions.explaination: A 16-bit instruction space has $2^{16} = 65536$ encodings. Type-1: 4 instructions with $3 \times 4\text{-bit}$ registers consume $4 \times 2^{12} = 16384$. Type-2: 8 instructions with $2 \times 6\text{-bit}$ registers consume $8 \times 2^{12} = 32768$. Type-3: 14 instructions with 4-bit and 6-bit registers consume $14 \times 2^{10} = 14336$. Remaining encodings $= 65536 - (16384 + 32768 + 14336) = 2048$. Each Type-4 instruction uses one 6-bit register ($2^6 = 64$ encodings). Thus, maximum $N = 2048 / 64 = 32$.

options.B: There are no cross-edges in 𝐺 with respect to the tree 𝑇

questions.subtopic: Graph traversals, minimum spanning trees, shortest paths
questions.explaination: In a BFS tree $T$, any edge $(u, w)$ in $G$ must connect vertices whose BFS levels differ by at most 1 (i.e., $\text{level}(w) \le \text{level}(u) + 1$). A forward-edge in a DFS tree goes from ancestor $u$ to descendant $w$ with $\text{level}(w) \ge \text{level}(u) + 2$. If such an edge existed in $G$, BFS would explore $w$ directly from $u$ at depth $\text{level}(u) + 1$, contradicting the structure of $T$. Hence, no forward-edges can exist in $G$ with respect to $T$ (C is TRUE).

a 40-byte TCP header. The packet is forwarded to an IPv4 router that supports a Maximum
Transmission Unit (MTU) of 600 bytes. Assume that the length of the IP header in all the
outgoing fragments of this packet is 20 bytes. Assume that the fragmentation offset value
stored in the first fragment is 0.

questions.subtopic: Fragmentation and IP addressing, IPv4, CIDR notation
questions.explaination: Total payload to fragment $= 4500 - 20 = 4480$ bytes. With $\text{MTU} = 600$, maximum payload per fragment must be a multiple of 8: $\lfloor (600 - 20) / 8 \rfloor \times 8 = 72 \times 8 = 576$ bytes. Fragment 1 carries bytes 0 to 575 (offset 0). Fragment 2 carries bytes 576 to 1151 (offset $576/8 = 72$). Fragment 3 carries bytes 1152 onwards, so its fragment offset field is $\frac{1152}{8} = 144$.

Consider the data transfer using TCP over a 1 Gbps link. Assuming that the
maximum segment lifetime (MSL) is set to 60 seconds, the minimum number of
bits required for the sequence number field of the TCP header, to prevent the
sequence number space from wrapping around during the MSL is____________.
questions.subtopic: Transport layer: flow control and congestion control, UDP, TCP, sockets

The sequence number space must satisfy $2^k \ge 7.5 \times 10^9$. Since $2^{32} \approx 4.29 \times 10^9 < 7.5 \times 10^9$ and $2^{33} \approx 8.59 \times 10^9 > 7.5 \times 10^9$, at least 33 bits are required.

Suppose in a web browser, you click on the www.gate-2023.in URL. The browser
cache is empty. The IP address for this URL is not cached in your local host, so
a DNS lookup is triggered (by the local DNS server deployed on your local host)
over the 3-tier DNS hierarchy in an iterative mode. No resource records are cached
anywhere across all DNS servers.
Let RTT denote the round trip time between your local host and DNS servers
in the DNS hierarchy. The round trip time between the local host and the web
server hosting www.gate-2023.in is also equal to RTT. The HTML ﬁle associated
with the URL is small enough to have negligible transmission time and negligible
rendering time by your web browser, which references 10 equally small objects on
the same web server.

time between clicking on the URL and your browser fully rendering it?

options.B: 5 RTTs, in case of persistent HTTP with pipelining.
options.C: 9 RTTs, in case of non-persistent HTTP with 5 parallel TCP connections.

questions.subtopic: Fragmentation and IP addressing, IPv4, CIDR notation
questions.explaination: At Router-1, max payload per fragment is $\lfloor (5000 - 20) / 8 \rfloor \times 8 = 4976$ bytes. 15000 bytes payload is fragmented into payloads of 4976, 4976, 4976, and 72 bytes (4 fragments). At Router-2 ($\text{MTU} = 3000$, max payload $\lfloor 2980/8 \rfloor \times 8 = 2976$ bytes), each of the three 4976-byte fragments splits into 2 fragments ($2976 + 2000$), yielding $3 \times 2 = 6$ fragments. The 72-byte fragment passes through intact. Total delivered fragments = $6 + 1 = 7$.
